title: Braid-like moves can be performed at height zero
statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Any two diagrams of the same oriented link can be
connected by a sequence of moves of the following kinds: braid isotopies of
closed braid diagrams, Markov stabilizations and destabilizations, and
Yamada-Vogel reducing moves and their inverses grouped into sequences with
positive-height intermediate diagrams; height-zero endpoints of these sequences
are allowed. Moreover, every type I, braid-like type II and braid-like type
III move occurring in such a sequence may be assumed to be performed at height
zero, that is, as a braid isotopy or as a stabilization.
strategy: Use a local Seifert-strip/gluing argument to find reductions avoiding an RI-adding/braid-likeII/III disk: a defect region cut by the local disk cannot be glued from outside pieces with at most one coherent pair, because uncut strips only join pieces exposing the same coherent pair. Thus some outside piece has an incoherent pair and supplies a reduction. Do not assert arbitrary-finite-subpicture avoidance. Push t down by the commuting r,t,r inverse sequence, and reverse for RI deletion. At height zero, II/III are braid isotopies. For a kink on another strand, move beneath intervening strands, stabilize at the axis, and return the kink by III_b plus inverse reducing moves, applying the pushing construction to new II/III content. Split reducing content at height zero; interiors positive, endpoints zero allowed. The local strip model and RI returning-crossing orientation verification must receive mathematical review before acceptance.

references.title: Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
